intro: Here, in Eskişehir province, lies Pessinus, an ancient city whose story runs from the 8th century BC to the 4th century AD. This was the cult centre of the Mother Goddess Cybele, and the holiest city of the Phrygians.
history: Pessinus was the homeland of the Cybele cult and the holiest city of Phrygia, and its fame reached all the way to Rome. In 205 BC the Romans resolved to carry off the city's sacred black stone to secure victory over Hannibal; in 204 BC the stone arrived in Rome. Yet Pessinus did not fade: it remained important under Galatian and Roman rule.
structure-1: You are now at the Temple of Cybele, a sacred building dedicated to the Mother Goddess. Pause here for a moment, in the presence of the goddess this city honoured.
structure-3: Now the Underground Galleries: secret passages leading out from the city walls. Imagine slipping through the dark, unseen, beyond the fortifications.
structure-4: Here stand the Hellenistic Walls, the city's fortifications, built in the Hellenistic period. Look closely at the stones that once guarded the holy city.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Theatre and the Colonnaded Street.
facts: Did you know? When the Romans carried Cybele's sacred black stone from here to Rome, it marked the first transfer of an Anatolian cult to the capital. Pessinus was the sanctuary of Cybele, and in 204 BC, following a prophecy meant to defeat Hannibal, Rome took the goddess's sacred black stone away to the capital. The marble steps in front of the sanctuary served both as a ceremonial stair and as theatre seating. And the stream that divides the city was channelled in antiquity between marble-faced banks.
outro: This brings our journey through Pessinus to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
